transcript_header: Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Jamal Price (Redwood CSM); Laura Chen (GC, Stratagem), Priya Singh (CTO), Mark Rivera (Head of Platform), Samir Patel (Procurement)
transcript_summary: Procurement onboarding call to review MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing approval steps, and technical gating for Redwood Private vs Dedicated deployment options.
Key concerns: data residency, KMS/encryption, SOC2 & audit logs, SLA uptime/latency guarantees, pricing approvals and PO timing.
Agreement on next steps: Redwood to send redline-ready MSA/DPA and SOC2 artifacts; SE to run benchmark; customer to confirm procurement timeline and redlines.
transcript_body: [00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone thanks for making time, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, joining with Ethan and Jamal. Good afternoon all.
[00:07] Laura Chen: Hi Sofia, thanks. Laura here. We're running a bit late, appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hey team, Priya here. I'll jump in on the architecture questions and timing.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir from procurement. Main goal today is to map out the legal path and approvals so we can onboard by end of Q2 if possible.
[00:25] Mark Rivera: Mark — head of platform — want to understand the Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and SLOs.
[00:31] Ethan Cole: Great. Quick agenda: MSA/DPA review process, SLA targets & metrics, KMS & data residency, pricing approvals and next steps. We'll keep it flexible.
[00:45] Sofia Martinez: Laura, what's your usual redlining cycle on MSAs? Do you need a fully executed DPA before demos or just during procurement?
[00:53] Laura Chen: We usually want the DPA in a signed state before we feed production data. For PoC we can do a mutual NDA and limited data but procurement wants the legal stack asap.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: Understood. We'll attach our standard DPA and SOC2 Type II reports. Ethan can speak to encryption and KMS options.

[01:12] Ethan Cole: Yep. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and HSM integrations. For Dedicated hosted we offer KMS integration via customer key in our VPC offering or managed keys depending on the plan.
[01:25] Mark Rivera: Can you confirm if the KV cache or prefix caching stores any PSI or PII? We need clarity on in-memory vs persisted caching.

[01:32] Ethan Cole: Good question. Our KV cache is in-memory on the inference nodes; for Dedicated it's isolated to your pool. Nothing persisted to shared storage unless you enable explicit checkpointing. Sorry sometimes the transcript tech says K V cash which is always fun.
[01:47] Priya Singh: Ok so for regulated workflows we prefer Private — on-prem or VPC — because of data residency. Does Redwood Private support air-gapped on-prem installs?

[01:56] Ethan Cole: Yes — we offer a private bundle that can be deployed on-prem with an optional offline installer; it's a bit of a longer runway (4–8 weeks) for validation. We'll include the install checklist.
[02:10] Samir Patel: Timing is critical. Our procurement needs cost certainty. What's the pricing approval path and contract length options?

[02:18] Sofia Martinez: We support monthly reserved capacity or annual commitments for Dedicated. Pricing tiers reflect qps and token volumes; I will send the pricing deck. For Private, it's typically an enterprise license plus support and a deployment fee.
[02:30] Samir Patel: Do you require a purchase order or is a signed SOW enough?
[02:33] Jamal Price: Typically we accept a PO or a signed order form under the MSA. We'll work with you on the billing flow that meets your finance org.
[02:42] Laura Chen: On the MSA, our legal team will want to adjust liability caps and data breach notification timelines. Can you highlight which clauses are negotiable?
[02:50] Sofia Martinez: Absolutely — we expect typical redlines around liability and indemnity. We'll flag the negotiable clauses when we send the MSA so you can prioritize.

[03:00] Ethan Cole: On SLA specifics — our Dedicated product has an SLA for availability and tail latency SLOs. We can commit to X% uptime for the dedicated pool and escalation paths. For Private we provide support SLAs tied to the support tier in the ent agreement.
[03:15] Mark Rivera: Can you quantify the latency SLO? Our UX 95th percentile needs to stay under 400ms for short prompts. How does batching affect that?

[03:23] Ethan Cole: With conservative batching and our GPU kernel selection, we typically see 95th pct in the 200–350ms range for 1k token bursts on Dedicated. If you need guaranteed 95th under 400ms at load we'll run workload-specific benchmarks. We'll also share the model profiles.
[03:40] Priya Singh: We also need audit logs and traceability for requests — does Redwood keep token-level audit logs and for how long?

[03:47] Jamal Price: We capture request metadata and have configurable retention. For hosted we default to 90 days; Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and push logs to customer-managed SIEM.
[03:58] Laura Chen: Regarding encryption — at-rest and in-transit are required, but we need to confirm key control for Private. Also, do you support SAML-based SSO and RBAC?

[04:07] Ethan Cole: Yes to both. SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access control — we support granular roles. For KMS, Private allows customer-key management. We'll include architecture docs.
[04:20] Samir Patel: On the procurement checklist, what is typically the longest blocker — legal review, security verification, or invoice/payment?

[04:27] Sofia Martinez: Often it's legal redlines plus security review; SOC2 and penetration test artifacts usually unblock security. Procurement and finance move quickly once legal and security sign off.
[04:35] Priya Singh: To expedite, can we run a short technical POC on Dedicated while legal finishes the DPA? We can use synthetic data or tokenized test dataset.
[04:43] Sofia Martinez: Yes — we can run a limited PoC under an NDA and scoped data. We'll send a PoC checklist and PoC order form.
[04:50] Ethan Cole: For the PoC please send sample traffic patterns — sequence lengths, expected qps, and any custom tokenization steps. We'll mirror your workload when we run the perf tests.
[05:02] Mark Rivera: What's the rollback / failover story if you have a regional outage? Any automatic fallback to another region or model variant?

[05:09] Ethan Cole: Our smart routing supports fallback to another capacity zone or to a lower-cost model variant if configured. For Dedicated customers we can set multi-region replication for the pool. We'll include a DR playbook.
[05:20] Laura Chen: Are there any audit requirements on our side to host keys if we do BYOK?
[05:24] Jamal Price: We typically provide guidance in the KMS integration doc; you maintain control of keys in your HSM and we'll never have access to unwrapped keys.
[05:31] Priya Singh: On cost modeling — can you provide a sample cost breakdown for 100k tokens/day with 3 models (one base gen, one chat, one embeddings)?
[05:39] Sofia Martinez: Yes — I'll attach a cost model spreadsheet. We'll include assumptions about batching, cache hit rates, and quantization options that affect unit cost.
[05:46] Mark Rivera: Speaking of quantization — will that impact quality or inference speed for our use case?

[05:50] Ethan Cole: There are tradeoffs: 4-bit quantization can reduce cost significantly with small quality delta for many workloads, but we'd validate on your prompts. We'll recommend quant profiles.
[05:58] Samir Patel: Any surprises on the MSA around insurance or SOC that we should prepare for?
[06:03] Sofia Martinez: We provide SOC2 Type II, penetration test summary, and cyber insurance details. If you need a vendor risk questionnaire answered we'll complete that too.
[06:12] Laura Chen: Can we get a redlineable MSA PDF and DPA doc so our team can start annotating?
[06:17] Sofia Martinez: Yes — we'll send Word/PDF redline-friendly versions. Expect the package with SOC2 and the security questionnaire link.
[06:24] Priya Singh: For onboarding, who is the technical owner on Redwood's side and what's the expected touchpoints?
[06:29] Jamal Price: Ethan will be the technical lead for the PoC and Jamal (CSM) will coordinate onboarding and ops.
[06:36] Ethan Cole: We'll set up a runbook: initial setup, perf benchmark, security sign-off, and cutover plan. We'll include times for a 1-week validation window if you choose Dedicated.
[06:46] Mark Rivera: One more on SLAs — do you provide credits for missed SLOs and what's the claim process?
[06:52] Sofia Martinez: Yes we provide SLA credits per the MSA; the claim process involves support ticketing and root cause analysis. We'll highlight that clause in the draft.
[07:01] Laura Chen: On data residency — we need to ensure all processing for EU customers stays in EU. Can Redwood pin regions?
[07:07] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we can pin requests to region-specific capacity pools. For Private on-prem it's fully resident. We'll include region pinning docs.
[07:15] Samir Patel: For approvals — our finance wants a 3-line summary of expected annual cost and a renewal schedule. Can you provide?
[07:21] Sofia Martinez: I'll prepare a one-pager with estimated spend, renewal terms, and support tiers.
[07:27] Priya Singh: If we find quality regressions post-rollout, do you have rollback and model pinning?
[07:32] Ethan Cole: Yes — model versioning and automatic fallback policies. We'll show you the console flow.
[07:38] Mark Rivera: Are there any export controls or restrictions we should be aware of for models?
[07:42] Jamal Price: We'll include export control guidance; most open models are fine but depending on data type there may be compliance constraints.
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: Ok quick recap: Redwood sends MSA/DPA + SOC2 and security package; SE runs bench; customer legal to redline; procurement to share PO flow and timeline. Any additions?
[07:58] Laura Chen: That covers it. We'll focus on liability caps and data residency redlines.
[08:03] Samir Patel: I'll get you the vendor onboarding checklist and estimated PO approval timeline by next week.
[08:08] Priya Singh: We'll schedule a tech deep-dive once we get the perf numbers.
[08:12] Sofia Martinez: Great — I'll send the follow-up email with attachments and proposed times for the exec sign-off. Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Meeting ends
